ga.heading: General and administrative expenses
ga.text: General and administrative expenses increased $14.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily driven by a $3.1 million increase in subscription, bank and network, depreciation and amortization and other general and administrative expenses, a $3.0 million increase in professional services expense, a $2.7 million increase in transaction-related incentives, a $2.2 million increase in restructuring expenses, a $1.9 million increase in compensation and benefit expenses (including $2.4 million of stock-based compensation expense related to founder equity awards resulting from the voluntary cancellations of outstanding unvested equity awards), and a $1.3 million increase in marketing expense, partially offset by a $0.1 million decrease in travel expense.

tax.text: The Pillar 2 approach, which came into effect in 2023 in certain jurisdictions, will establish a global minimum tax rate of 15%, such that multinational enterprises with an effective tax rate in a jurisdiction below this minimum rate will need to pay additional tax. While many aspects of the application of Pillar 2 remain to be clarified, including how the jurisdictions in which we operate, and those in which we and our subsidiaries are based, choose to implement the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development’s approach in their tax treaties and domestic tax laws, we do not expect Pillar 2 to apply in 2026. On July 4, 2025, the "One Big Beautiful Bill Act" (P.L. 119‑21) was enacted into law. The legislation reinstates and extends several provisions of the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, including permanent 100% bonus depreciation, enhanced Section 179 expensing, full R&D expense deduction for domestic expenditures and modification to the international tax framework.

ocf.heading: Net Cash Used In Operating Activities
ocf.text: Net cash used in operating activities increased by $62.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily driven by a $102.3 million increase in net loss, a $22.4 million increase in deferred tax benefit, a $20.4 million gain on extinguishment of debt, a $12.1 million increase in other current assets, a $7.0 million increase in prepaid expenses, a $4.3 million increase in accounts receivable, a $3.9 million decrease in accounts payable, a $3.9 million increase in staking and other income, and a $1.5 million increase in accrued interest income, partially offset by a $76.7 million increase in net loss on digital assets, a $24.6 million decrease in operating activities settled in digital assets and stablecoins, a $4.9 million increase in payroll liabilities, a $3.7 million decrease in income tax receivable, a $2.3 million increase in stock-based compensation expense, a $2.0 million increase in loss (gain) on disposed investments, and $1.6 million of other items, net.

da.text: Digital asset services expenses increased $0.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily driven by a $1.4 million increase in restructuring expenses, a $0.9 million increase in technology subscription expense, a $0.5 million increase in fiat onboarding costs, a $0.3 million decrease in capitalized labor, and a $0.3 million increase in testing expense, partially offset by a $2.4 million decrease in salary and benefit expenses, a $0.6 million decrease in cloud infrastructure expense, and a $0.3 million decrease in depreciation and amortization expense.

net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text:
Revenue increased $2.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily driven by a $10.9 million increase in revenue contributed by the Acquired Entities within payment processing services, partially offset by an $8.7 million decrease in revenue from digital asset services, primarily attributable to an $8.1 million decrease in exchange aggregation revenue due to lower volume.

Revenue decreased $10.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. The decrease was primarily driven by a $26.5 million decrease in revenue from digital asset services, primarily attributable to a $26.6 million decrease in exchange aggregation revenue due to lower volume, partially offset by a $15.9 million increase in revenue contributed by the Acquired Entities within payment processing services.

Digital asset services.heading: Digital asset services expenses
Digital asset services.text:
Digital asset services expenses increased $0.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily driven by a $1.4 million increase in restructuring expenses, a $0.9 million increase in technology subscription expense, a $0.5 million increase in fiat onboarding costs, a $0.3 million decrease in capitalized labor, and a $0.3 million increase in testing expense, partially offset by a $2.4 million decrease in salary and benefit expenses, a $0.6 million decrease in cloud infrastructure expense, and a $0.3 million decrease in depreciation and amortization expense.

Digital asset services expenses increased $2.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily driven by a $1.8 million increase in fiat onboarding costs, a $1.4 million increase in restructuring expenses, a $0.7 million increase in technology subscription expense, a $0.4 million decrease in capitalized labor, and a $0.2 million increase in salary and benefit expenses, partially offset by a $1.2 million decrease in depreciation and amortization expense, a $0.7 million decrease in cloud infrastructure expense, a $0.4 million decrease in consulting expense, and a $0.1 million decrease in testing expense.

Payment processing services.text: The acquisitions of the Acquired Entities represent a significant milestone in the Company's evolution, expanding its enterprise offerings, diversifying its revenue base, and adding payment processing services and customer programs that complement its existing digital asset services.

intro.text: Founded in 2015, Exodus Movement, Inc. (NYSE American: EXOD) is pioneering self-custodial finance by giving people the tools to earn rewards, spend, manage, and swap digital assets across borders, all without giving up control. Exodus serves millions of users through its products built on a simple principle: your money should be yours. Exodus also powers crypto infrastructure and card/payment services for enterprise platforms serving millions of users through its enterprise product suite. Headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska, Exodus is financial software where ownership is the default. For more information, visit exodus.com.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
